# 1 Clement Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 6

**6:1** Alongside these holy men, a great crowd of God's chosen were gathered in — people who suffered many humiliations and tortures through jealousy, and in doing so set a magnificent example right here among us.

**6:2** Women too were persecuted because of jealousy. Forced to play the roles of Danaids and Dirces, they endured horrifying and degrading torments. But though their bodies were frail, they ran the race of faith to the finish and received the noble prize.

**6:3** Jealousy has torn wives away from their husbands, twisting the meaning of what our father Adam said: "This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh." [Gen 2:23]

**6:4** Jealousy and strife have toppled great cities and uprooted powerful nations.

---

*PNEUMA note: "Danaids and Dirces" — in the Neronian persecution, Christian women were reportedly executed in the arena while costumed as mythological women condemned to eternal punishment: Danaids (water-carriers), Dirces (tied to bulls). See Tacitus, Annals 15.44.*
